title: The Mattila-Sjölin problem for the k-distance over a finite field
summary: Let $\mathbb{F}_q^d$ be a $d$-dimensional vector space over a finite field $\mathbb{F}_q$ with $q$ elements. For $x\in \mathbb{F}_q^d$, let $\|x\| = x_1^2+\dots+x_d^2$. By abuse of terminology, we shall call $\|\cdot\|$ a norm on $\mathbb{F}_q^d$. For a subset $E\subset \mathbb{F}_q^d$, let $Δ(E)$ be the distance set on $E$ defined as $Δ(E):=\{\|x-y\| : x, y \in E \}$. The Mattila-Sjölin problem seeks the smallest exponent $α>0$ such that $Δ(E) =\mathbb{F}_q$ for all subsets $E \subset \mathbb{F}_q^d$ with $|E| \geq Cq^α$.
